messages:
diana: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about manifest stitching for sealed bundles in air-gapped installs. we currently do index-first + chunked fetch, but customers hit OOMs when they try to stream large model packs. thoughts on moving more stitching work to the server-side vs client-side?

alex: Server-side stitching would save client memory but increases bundle server CPU and state. for disconnected gateways it also means we need a trusted stitch service in the airgap gateway image.

kevin: +1 on server-side for low-power endpoints. tradeoff: increases attack surface for signature verification timing. we should keep final signature check client-side.

maya: If we do server-side, can we emit a compact index that the client can validate cheaply? e.g., layered Merkle summary per chunk so client only keeps O(1) metadata in RAM.

diana: exact idea I had. compact summary + per-chunk merkle proofs. client verifies root sig and then incremental chunk proofs as they arrive. avoids keeping whole index.

jon: What about resumability? customers often lose network during seed transfer. We need deterministic byte-range resume and chunk checksums. maybe align chunking to 4MB boundaries so both server and client can resume with range requests.

alex: Agree on fixed chunk size for simpler resume. Also consider a "manifest-of-manifests" approach: top-level small manifest lists component manifests (model, runtime, hooks). client can request only needed components first. reduces peak disk.

ops: infra note: any server-side stitching needs a fallback to client-stitch mode for airgap customers who run older gateway images. we can't force a gateway upgrade in many regulated installs.

kevin: Fallback + capability negotiation at handshake time. gateway reports capabilities in the seed handshake: `client.capabilities = ["stitching:v2", "range-resume"]`. server picks best transfer plan.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new canary of gateway image with stitching service pushed to canary fleet (tag: stitch-v2-canary). monitor for memory/CPU churn.

maya: Telemetry: emit per-chunk transfer timings + verify time + resume count. we can use that to suggest chunk-size heuristics per site. keep telemetry opt-in for airgapped installs (store locally and allow upload via ops).

diana: Security: always verify signatures before activation. even if server stitches, client must compute root hash and run `verify(root.sig)`. if mismatch, abort and report. Also add a short TTL for server-supplied stitch plans to avoid replay.

jon: Rollback markers: include an activation manifest that lists previous active version ID. agent should write a durable rollback token before switching. if activation fails, run revert using token. keep this separate from bundle content to avoid bundle corruption.

alex: small ergonomic note: provide a `--dry-run` mode in the upgrader that simulates stitch+verify without writing to disk so ops can validate size/space beforehand.

diana: Implementation plan summary: 1) capability negotiation + feature flags, 2) server-side optional stitching with compact merkle proofs, 3) fixed chunk size + range-resume, 4) activation/rollback token write, 5) telemetry aggregator (opt-in). sounds good? :thumbsup:

kevin: yes, and add explicit fallback to client-stitching when server returns 503 or unsupported.

maya: will draft follow-up RFC with proto for compact summary and proof messages. I'll add a sample wire format and a tiny pseudocode verify snippet.

diana: awesome — post the RFC here and tag @kevin and @alex for review. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
